title: Is the Treasury convenience yield rebounding?
gist: The option-adjusted spread of the ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index, a proxy for the Treasury convenience yield, has widened from 30 bp on October 8, 2025 to 41 bp on September 25, 2026, suggesting a partial recovery in the Treasury convenience yield. The spread is still below its 2012-19 average of 67 bp, and part of the widening may reflect corporate credit risk and liquidity rather than Treasury benefits.

insights.claim: The Treasury convenience yield is investors' willingness to accept lower yields on US Treasuries in exchange for non-interest benefits such as safety and ease of trading.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: A shrinking convenience yield signals erosion of Treasuries' special safe-haven/liquidity status, which would raise US government financing costs.
insights.quote: Investors’ willingness to accept lower yields in exchange for these benefits is known as the Treasury convenience yield.
insights.locator: US Treasury securities offer investors benefits

insights.claim: The option-adjusted spread of the ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index, which compares yields on the highest-rated corporate bonds to the Treasury curve after adjusting for embedded options, serves as one proxy for the Treasury convenience yield.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: Investors can track the AAA corporate-Treasury OAS as a real-time gauge of Treasury 'specialness'.
insights.quote: This measure compares yields on the highest-rated corporate bonds with a Treasury yield curve, adjusting for options embedded in the corporate bonds.

insights.claim: Changes in the AAA corporate-Treasury spread cannot be attributed entirely to the Treasury convenience yield because the spread also reflects corporate credit risk and liquidity conditions.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: Wider AAA spreads may partly signal rising credit risk or tighter liquidity, not just restored Treasury demand; cross-check with other measures.
insights.quote: the spread also reflects corporate credit risk and liquidity conditions, so its increase cannot be attributed entirely to changes in the benefits of holding Treasuries.
insights.locator: These movements suggest a partial recovery

insights.claim: The AAA corporate-Treasury option-adjusted spread averaged 67 basis points during 2012-19 but only 36 basis points from the start of 2025 through October 8, 2025, documenting a decline in the Treasury convenience yield.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: Treasuries' premium over top-rated corporates roughly halved versus the pre-pandemic norm, consistent with diminished Treasury specialness.
insights.quote: It averaged 67 basis points during 2012-19, compared with 36 basis points from the beginning of 2025 through October 8, 2025.

insights.claim: On October 8, 2025, the AAA corporate-Treasury option-adjusted spread stood at 30 basis points, which the FRED Blog uses as its benchmark low point.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: The 30 bp level is the reference for judging whether the convenience yield is recovering.
insights.quote: The green dashed line marks the spread’s value on that date: 30 basis points, or 0.30 percentage points.

insights.claim: The AAA corporate-Treasury spread widened unevenly after October 2025: it reached 45 basis points in March 2026, narrowed to 32 basis points in May 2026, and rose to 46 basis points in July 2026.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: The recovery is volatile rather than a steady trend, so single readings should not be over-interpreted.
insights.quote: It reached 45 basis points in March 2026, narrowed to 32 basis points in May, and rose to 46 basis points in July.
insights.locator: Since then, the spread has widened

insights.claim: On September 25, 2026, the AAA corporate-Treasury spread was 41 basis points, 11 basis points above the October 2025 benchmark of 30 basis points but still below the 2012-19 average of 67 basis points.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
entities: ICE BofA AAA U.S. Corporate Index
insights.so_what: Roughly 30% of the gap to the pre-pandemic norm has been closed; Treasury specialness remains impaired.
insights.quote: On September 25, it stood at 41 basis points: 11 basis points above the October 2025 benchmark, but still below the 2012-19 average.
insights.locator: Since then, the spread has widened

insights.claim: The widening of the AAA corporate-Treasury spread since October 2025 suggests a partial, not full, recovery in the Treasury convenience yield.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Demand for Treasuries' safety and liquidity may be recovering, modestly easing concerns about erosion of their safe-asset status.
insights.quote: The spread between AAA corporate bonds and Treasuries has widened since October 2025, suggesting a partial recovery in the Treasury convenience yield.
